title: 02. Tool Calling & MCP: Day 11 — Tools & Retrieval
summary: Today you graduate from "prompt in, text out" agents to tool-calling agents that act on the world.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.body:
Today you graduate from "prompt in, text out" agents to **tool-calling agents** that act on the world. A tool is a Python function the model can decide to invoke; the framework converts your function's signature into a JSON schema the model is trained to call. This unlocks agents that book meetings, search docs, query databases, and write files — not just talk about doing so.

You will build two complete agents:

1. **Calendar Helper** (LangChain) — `@tool` decorator plus `create_tool_calling_agent` and `AgentExecutor`. The agent schedules events, lists them, and finds free slots, all from natural-language requests.
2. **Knowledge Base Search** (Pydantic AI) — `@agent.tool` with a `RunContext[DocStore]` dependency. The agent searches a hardcoded set of markdown policy docs and answers with citations.

The contrast is the lesson: LangChain treats tools as plain callables bound to the agent, Pydantic AI treats them as methods on a typed dependency container. Both end up calling the same underlying model APIs.

sections.title: Common Pitfalls
sections.body:
**Forgetting `agent_scratchpad` in the LangChain prompt.** The placeholder `MessagesPlaceholder(variable_name="agent_scratchpad")` is mandatory for `create_tool_calling_agent`. Without it you get a cryptic `KeyError` on the first tool call. The scratchpad is where the framework writes the `ToolMessage` results back so the model can see them on its next iteration.

**Tool docstrings that are too terse.** Models decide whether to call a tool based on its name and docstring. `"""Add event."""` is too thin — the model will not know what date format to pass. Always document parameter formats and intent, and prefer concrete examples in the docstring.

**Returning non-string from a Pydantic AI tool.** Pydantic AI serializes return values, but complex nested objects can confuse some models. Stick to `str`, `list[dict]`, or simple Pydantic models. If you need to return a rich object, convert to a flat dict with primitive fields.

**Using module-level mutable state for storage.** Both projects above do this for brevity, and it's fine for a single-process demo. In tests, in CI with parallel workers, or in production, this causes flaky failures. Day 12 introduces LangGraph checkpointer state; for Pydantic AI, prefer the `deps` pattern even for "just a dict."

**Tool name collisions.** If two tools have similar names (`search` vs `search_docs`), the model sometimes calls the wrong one. Use verb-noun names like `add_event`, `list_events`, `find_free_slot`. Avoid Python keywords or builtins as tool names.

**Passing `ctx` incorrectly.** In Pydantic AI, the first parameter of an `@agent.tool` must be `ctx: RunContext[Deps]` — never the query. If you accidentally write `def search_docs(query: str)` without `ctx`, you'll get a registration error. Use `@agent.tool_plain` for tools that don't need the deps or context.
